class.name: Rogue
class.text: Energy is the whole class, and combo points are what you spend it on. Sinister Strike, Eviscerate and Stealth are yours from the start, Sprint, Slice and Dice and Sap come at 10, Shank at 24. Every line below is a strike, a finisher or a way out.

card.caresAbout: Energy, combo points, which way the monster faces, and what is ready
card.vocabulary: strike, open, finish, points, Energy, behind, Stealth, slip away
card.soundsLike: quiet and exact, a trainer who counts out loud. A rogue line says where to stand before it says what to press
card.neverSays: mana, rage, cast, anything mystical ("shadows", "deadly", "silent"), and boasting about backstabs
card.test: could it be said in one breath before the pull?

advice.say: Combat is the build this page advises, because it is the smoothest to level, with Riposte at 20 and Blade Flurry at 30. The price: it wants a sword, axe or mace more than a dagger. Assassination wants daggers and is slow until Mutilate at 42. Subtlety is sturdy and slow to kill.

overview.who: You open on a monster before it knows you are there, build combo points with strikes and spend them on a finisher. The craft is picking the fight, and knowing when to leave it.
overview.good: Damage on one monster at a time, stuns and a sap to hold a fight still, and ways out: Vanish, Sprint, Evasion. You also skip fights by sneaking past what you do not want.
overview.bad: Being hit for long, and crowds. You wear leather and cannot heal, and you hurt one monster at a time. Bandages are your healing.
overview.resource: Energy, which fills back by itself, and combo points, which stay on the monster you built them on. Spend Energy on strikes, spend points on a finisher, and do not sit at full Energy.
overview.levelling: Strike to build points, finish with Eviscerate or Slice and Dice, bandage between pulls. Learn First Aid early, it heals faster than eating. Sneak past what you can.
overview.ten: You get your first talent point and pick a spec. Combat is the one most guides level. Assassination and Subtlety are the other two, and a respec costs gold.

damage.reason: Most guides level Combat. Riposte hits hard from 20 and Blade Flurry takes two monsters at once from 30.

builds.name: Assassination
builds.intro: Assassination lives on poisons and Mutilate, which comes at 42. Until then it plays like any rogue with a dagger. Guides call it a slow way to level, and guides want a dagger in each hand.
builds.line: Poisons, Shank and Mutilate with daggers. Slow until 42, then the hardest single hits.
builds.pathNote: (34 points in Assassination, then 12 in Combat and 5 in Subtlety.)
builds.split: the whole order. Mobalytics' Djexde gives the only full order and says to level Combat instead. Icy Veins names the same key talents (Remorseless Attacks, Ruthlessness, Relentless Strikes, Lethality, Cold Blood, Seal Fate, Venom) but its order sits in a slider that could not be read. Method, as read, prefers Assassination.
builds.dry: A monster immune to poison takes Mutilate at its plain damage.

path.why: After a kill, your next strike is more likely to crit for a short time. Go straight to the next monster and it pays.
Sinister Strike costs less Energy, and you press it until Mutilate. A cheap strike lets you press more of them.
More critical strikes with every attack and poison. Critical hits are where a rogue's damage comes from.
Slice and Dice lasts longer, so you refresh it less and strike more.
More critical strikes with every attack and poison. Critical hits are where a rogue's damage comes from.
A bigger Energy bar. You can spend more before you have to wait.
Your finishers sometimes add a combo point to the monster, so the next finisher comes sooner.
Your next strike or Eviscerate is a certain critical hit. Keep it for the hit that matters, and press it again when it is ready.
Poisons land more often and sometimes spend no charge, so you coat your weapons less.
Shank also raises your poison damage and how often poisons land for a few seconds. Mutilate needs it, so it comes before Mutilate.
Finishers sometimes give back 25 Energy, more often the more points they spend. More Energy means more strikes.
A critical hit from a strike sometimes adds another combo point, so finishers come sooner.
Finishers sometimes give back 25 Energy, more often the more points they spend. More Energy means more strikes.
Poisons land more often and sometimes spend no charge, so you coat your weapons less.
Hits with both weapons, harder on a poisoned monster, and gives 2 combo points. It replaces Sinister Strike and needs a dagger.
Eviscerate hits harder. It ends most fights, so this pays on every kill.
You parry more often, and a parry is what lights Riposte. Some hits simply stop landing.
Fewer misses. A strike that misses is Energy spent for nothing, and a rogue has little to spare.
After a parry, Riposte hits harder than a strike for little Energy and disarms the monster. Press it whenever it lights.
Fewer misses. A strike that misses is Energy spent for nothing, and a rogue has little to spare.
Backstab, Garrote, Ambush and Mutilate hit harder. Mutilate is your main strike, so most of it lands there.
Your poisons do more damage. A modest gain, taken last because the points have nowhere better to go.

builds.name: Combat
builds.intro: Combat swings two weapons and leans on Riposte, Shank and Blade Flurry. It is the build most guides level, because it is smooth and wastes little. Take a sword, axe or mace, and a dagger only if you must.
builds.line: Sinister Strike, Riposte after a parry, Blade Flurry for two. The smoothest way to level a rogue.
builds.pathNote: (35 points in Combat, then 16 in Assassination for critical hits and poisons.)
builds.split: the first points and the tail. DonTheCrown puts Precision at 2 first and reaches Riposte at 20 and Blade Flurry at 30, Djexde takes Remorseless Attacks first and reaches them at 22 and 32. This page follows DonTheCrown. Method would move points from Lightning Reflexes and Endurance into Puncturing Wounds for a dagger.
builds.dry: Riposte only lights after a parry, so face the monster and let it swing.

path.why: Sinister Strike costs less Energy, and it is the strike you press most. More of them land before the monster is dead.
Eviscerate hits harder. It ends most fights, so this pays on every kill.
Fewer misses. A strike that misses is Energy spent for nothing, and a rogue has little to spare.
You parry more often, and a parry is what lights Riposte. Some hits simply stop landing.
After a parry, Riposte hits harder than Sinister Strike for little Energy and disarms the monster. Press it whenever it lights.
Fewer misses. A strike that misses is Energy spent for nothing, and a rogue has little to spare.
Sprint and Evasion come back sooner. A rogue's way out is its cooldowns, so shorter ones mean more fights you can leave.
Sprint breaks slows and roots as you press it. A monster that slows you can no longer hold you in the fight.
Eviscerate costs less Energy, so you finish sooner and start the next strike sooner.
Fewer of your strikes are dodged or parried. Monsters in front of you do both often, so every point wastes less.
Sinister Strike and Eviscerate hit a little harder, and they are most of your damage.
Your swings come faster and each hit also strikes a second monster nearby. This is how a rogue takes two at once. Press it with Evasion.
Your off-hand hits harder. You swing two weapons all fight, so it pays on every swing.
Swords and axes sometimes swing again for free, daggers and fists add critical chance, maces ignore armour. Carry the weapon that fits it.
Shank gives back more Energy and comes round sooner. The more you press it, the less you wait.
A burst of Energy for a hard fight. Press it with Blade Flurry when your Energy is nearly empty.
More critical strikes with every attack and poison. Critical hits are where a rogue's damage comes from.
Your finishers sometimes add a combo point to the monster, so the next finisher comes sooner.
Slice and Dice lasts longer, so you refresh it less and strike more.
Critical hits from your strikes hurt more. It needs Malice at full, and Malice is worth having anyway.
Swords and axes sometimes swing again for free, daggers and fists add critical chance, maces ignore armour. Carry the weapon that fits it.
Sinister Strike and Eviscerate hit a little harder, and they are most of your damage.
Slice and Dice lasts longer, so you refresh it less and strike more.
Expose Armor costs less Energy and gives points back when cast at 5. Take it for the hard monsters.
Poisons land more often and sometimes spend no charge, so you coat your weapons less.

builds.name: Subtlety
builds.intro: Subtlety opens with Ambush and lives on Hemorrhage from 32. It is the sturdiest of the three at the start and the weakest on damage. The long way down the tree is the price.
builds.line: An Ambush opener, Ghostly Strike, Hemorrhage, then Death Mark at 42. Sturdy, and slower to kill.
builds.pathNote: (31 points in Subtlety, then 14 in Combat and 6 in Assassination.)
builds.split: the whole order. Mobalytics' Djexde gives a full order and advises Combat instead. Icy Veins agrees on the shape (Subtlety down to Hemorrhage, then Death Mark, then Combat, then Assassination) and its order sits in a slider that could not be read. Warcraft Tavern's Subtlety page and Kami Labs' simulation still use the talents removed before launch.
builds.dry: Backstab does nothing from the front, so walk round or use Hemorrhage.

path.why: After a kill, your next opener or strike is more likely to crit for a short time. It keeps you hitting hard between monsters.
You sometimes gain a combo point after a dodge. A small gain, taken because it opens the way down the tree.
Backstab, Garrote and Ambush hit harder. They are your openers, so every point counts.
Cheap Shot and Garrote cost less Energy, and Garrote no longer needs you behind the monster.
Backstab, Garrote and Ambush hit harder. They are your openers, so every point counts.
Your attacks ignore some armour and Rupture hits harder. It also leads to Hemorrhage.
Starts a fight with 2 combo points before the first strike. Press it just before Ambush or Garrote.
Ambush, Garrote and Cheap Shot each add a combo point more. The opener becomes the first finisher.
A strike that raises your dodge for a few seconds and lets Garrote or Ambush go without Stealth. Press it on cooldown.
Ambush, Garrote and Cheap Shot each add a combo point more. The opener becomes the first finisher.
Vanish and Blind come back much sooner. Your way out is ready for the next fight.
The build's main strike. It builds combo points with any weapon, from the front or behind, and makes your Rupture and Garrote hit harder.
Resets your cooldowns when a fight goes wrong, Evasion and Vanish with them. You hope not to press it, and Death Mark needs it.
A little less chance to be hit by spells and ranged attacks, and you spot hidden things sooner. Small, and it keeps the way down open.
You move faster in Stealth and Stealth is ready again sooner. Sneaking past monsters is how you skip fights.
Shank adds combo points to the monster every time. Press it on cooldown and your finishers come much sooner.
A finisher that stores your damage for a few seconds and then deals it. Use it on a long fight, with Garrote and Rupture bleeding.
Sinister Strike and Hemorrhage cost less Energy. Hemorrhage is your main strike, so this is the Energy you save most.
Eviscerate and Death Mark hit harder. Both end fights, so this pays on every kill.

stages.about: Poisons at 20, Premeditation at 25 and Ghostly Strike at 27 give you the opener. Hemorrhage at 32 is the strike you press from then on.

opening.if: before the pull, out of combat
opening.why: Poised takes Energy off your first ability

opening.name: Stealth
opening.if: before the pull, if you can reach it unseen
opening.why: you strike first and it has not seen you

opening.name: Premeditation
opening.if: just before the opener
opening.why: you start the fight with 2 combo points

opening.name: Ambush
opening.if: with a dagger, or Garrote on a long fight
opening.why: it is the hardest hit you have for a first strike

loop.name: Ghostly Strike
loop.why: you dodge more, and Garrote needs no Stealth

loop.name: Shank
loop.if: when it is ready and Energy is not full
loop.why: it gives back more Energy than it costs

loop.name: Slice and Dice
loop.why: your swings come faster for the whole fight

loop.name: Eviscerate
loop.if: at 5 combo points, near the end of the fight
loop.why: it spends the points on one big hit

loop.name: Hemorrhage
loop.why: it builds points with any weapon, from any side

loop.name: Sinister Strike
loop.why: it builds the points until Hemorrhage is yours

rarely.name: Backstab
rarely.if: when you are behind with a dagger
rarely.why: it hits hard and gives you a combo point

rarely.name: Rupture
rarely.if: at 5 points, on a monster that will last
rarely.why: it keeps hurting while you strike

rarely.name: Preparation
rarely.if: when a fight has gone wrong
rarely.why: it readies Evasion and Vanish again

rarely.name: Kick
rarely.if: when a monster starts a spell
rarely.why: it stops the cast

rarely.name: Vanish
rarely.if: when a fight goes wrong
rarely.why: the monster loses you and you can bandage

rarely.name: Kidney Shot
rarely.if: on a monster you cannot beat in the open
rarely.why: each point is a second of stun

rarely.name: Gouge
rarely.if: when a second monster joins
rarely.why: it holds one still while you kill the other

rarely.name: Evasion
rarely.if: when a monster hits hard
rarely.why: you dodge more while it lasts

rarely.name: Sap
rarely.if: on one of two humanoids, before the pull
rarely.why: it sleeps until something hurts it

rarely.name: Blind
rarely.if: to get away from a monster you cannot beat
rarely.why: it wanders off blind while you leave

between.why: each hit may poison, and it costs no Energy

between.if: after a fight, before the next pull
between.why: Energy comes back by itself, health does not
